L33@P1: 1. INTRODUCTION
L34@P1: The Diana children’s community services provide care to infants, children and young people
L35@P1: in their homes or in a non-hospital setting, such as education facilities including special
L36@P1: schools.
L37@P1: Many children in receipt of this care require support from medical devices to maintain their
L38@P1: health status. Early detection, timeliness, and competency of response to changes in
L39@P1: clinical observations are important determinants of clinical outcome in the event that health
L40@P1: status deteriorates during our care. This document was developed to ensure consistent
L41@P1: safe practice, ensuring safety is maintained, any after care is given including safe transfer
L42@P1: to hospital if this is needed.
L43@P1: 2. PURPOSE
L44@P1: Staff who are routinely providing this monitoring function are Specialist Practitioners and
L45@P1: Nursing Associates supported by Registered Nurses. Therefore this SOP is to provide a
L46@P1: safe local procedure for supporting all staff in Diana children’s community services to
L47@P1: effectively monitor the health status of children and young people. Children who are
L48@P1: becoming unwell may have abnormalities that are detectable by clinical observations in
L49@P1: advance of deterioration and can be recognised through monitoring of vital signs/clinical
L50@P1: observations.
L51@P1: This SOP will ensure a standardised approach to:
L52@P1: • Monitoring of vital signs
L53@P1: • Identifying normal parameters for respiratory rate, oxygen saturations, pulse rate and
L54@P1: temperature recordings
L55@P1: • When to report abnormalities and any immediate actions to be taken
L56@P1-2: • Using agreed medical devices for monitoring vital signs/clinical observationsINSERT [Title of SOP, Version & Date]
L57@P2: 3. SCOPE
L58@P2: The SOP is applicable to all Staff in the Diana Community Childrens Services.
L59@P2: To ensure that all infants, children and young persons in receipt of care from the Diana
L60@P2: service are managed safely and deterioration in health status is recognised and acted on
L61@P2: appropriately in a timely manner.
L62@P2: 4. ABBREVIATIONS & DEFINITIONS
L63@P2: CCT Continuing care team
L64@P2: ‘GETTING TO
L65@P2: KNOW’.
L66@P2: This is a term used by the Diana children’s community services The
L67@P2: purpose of the ‘getting to know’ is to enable the named nurse and
L68@P2: Key Workers to get an overview of the child’s routine, nursing care
L69@P2: and preferences that will be required during the service provision; as
L70@P2: well as the home environment in which they will be working. It also
L71@P2: allows the child and family time to get to know their key staff.
L72@P2: It is intended to provide guidance to minimise the risk of a delay in
L73@P2: service provision to the child and family, to support staff and child’s
L74@P2: safety and to identify essential competencies required for each
L75@P2: individual child’s care.
L76@P2: FYPC LDA Families young peoples, children’s, learning disability and autism
L77@P2: division.
L78@P2: SYSTMONE The electronic record keeping platform used by services in LPT.
L79@P2: NAMED NURSE The lead practitioner responsible for identifying the nursing care
L80@P2: required to maintain the health status of the child, developing care
L81@P2: plans to reflect this care and agreeing these with the child and family.
L82@P2: The named nurse will also identify the competency assessments
L83@P2: required by the key workers, ensure these are completed and that
L84@P2: appropriate care is provided by the key workers. The named nurse
L85@P2: also provides support and guidance to both the key workers and the
L86@P2: family regarding all aspects of the child’s nursing care.
L87@P2: SP Diana children’s services specialist practitioner
L88@P2: KEY WORKER Diana children’s services specialist practitioner / nursing associate
L89@P2: assigned to provide continuing care to a particular child and family.
L90@P2: RN registered nurse
L91@P2: NA Nursing associate
L92@P2: PYREXIA Body core temperature regarded as 37°C. Pyrexia (fever) is a rise
L93@P2: above 37°C
L94@P2-3: HYPOTHERMIA Hypothermia is a low body temperature below 35 °CINSERT [Title of SOP, Version & Date]
L95@P3: VITAL SIGNS /
L96@P3: CLINICAL
L97@P3: OBSERVATIONS
L98@P3: Clinical observation is defined as the measurements of the body’s
L99@P3: most basic functions temperature, pulse (H/R), oxygen saturation
L100@P3: and respiratory and from a patient in a healthcare setting. Clinical
L101@P3: observations may also be known as vital signs.
L102@P3: EPR Electronic patient record
L103@P3: TRAUMATIC
L104@P3: PETECHIAE
L105@P3: Petechiae are pinpoint non-blanching spots that measure less than 2
L106@P3: mm in size and affect the skin and mucous membranes. Petechial
L107@P3: rashes are common and can be a significant cause for concern for
L108@P3: parents and the interprofessional team. Petechial rashes result from
L109@P3: areas of haemorrhage into the dermis.
L110@P3: 5. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
L111@P3: The registered nurses as named nurses, NA’s and SP’s need to fulfil the duties outlined
L112@P3: in the process section of this document.
L113@P3: The Team Leaders and Clinical Leads need to support named nurses in their role and
L114@P3: support training and competence assessment for all staff.
L115@P3: RN’s, NA’s and SP’s need to maintain their own competence. Highlight any concerns
L116@P3: regarding their own competence with named nurse or on call staff when they arise and
L117@P3: keep the named nurses updated with any changes to the health status of the
L118@P3: child/young person.
L119@P3: 6. PROCESS
L120@P3: Routinely.
L121@P3: Observations of vital signs or clinical observations need to be monitored and recorded
L122@P3: routinely as dictated by the child or young person’s care plan.
L123@P3: When a child or young person is unwell.
L124@P3: Observations of vital signs or clinical observations will also need to be monitored and
L125@P3: recorded more frequently than routine care plan dictates if the child or young person is
L126@P3: unwell. Often, parents will initially alert staff of the need to perform this, SP’s and NA’s
L127@P3: need to report and discuss this with the named nurse if on duty or the coordinator or
L128@P3: nurse on call if out of hours. If this occurs out of hours the on-call nurse will need to be
L129@P3: contacted to discuss frequency and appropriateness. If this is a child in school, Diana
L130@P3: School Nursing Team staff may be asked to record observations to determine the
L131@P3: health status of the child before they report to their team leader their concerns or prior
L132@P3: to telephoning parents or for an ambulance.
L133@P3: The child, young person and or parent/carer should consent to vital signs monitoring. In
L134@P3-4: School staff will do this as a duty of care as they act in loco parentis.INSERT [Title of SOP, Version & Date]
L135@P4: Where appropriate, the child, young person and parent or carer should be given the
L136@P4: opportunity to assist the practitioner in performing vital sign monitoring and
L137@P4: measurement.
L138@P4: All staff within the CCT team will spend a period of at least 4 weeks getting to know
L139@P4: every child in their care, in this period they will learn what is ‘normal’ for the specific
L140@P4: child, making it easier to determine any deviation from the norm indicating possible
L141@P4: illness. Staff within the special schools will get to know young people on getting to know
L142@P4: visits and will take direction from school staff who are their main carers at School.
L143@P4: RESPIRATORY RATE.
L144@P4: An elevated respiration rate is a powerful sign of acute illness and distress in all
L145@P4: children and young people, as is a reduced respiratory an indicator of central nervous
L146@P4: system depression.
L147@P4: Respiratory rate should be recorded for 60 seconds to account for variations in
L148@P4: respiratory rate and pattern.
L149@P4: Depth, symmetry and pattern of respiration should also be noted and recorded if
L150@P4: abnormal together with any associate sounds e.g., wheeze, cough and should form part
L151@P4: of any assessment.
L152@P4: Any deviation from identified normal parameters should prompt immediate discussion
L153@P4: with named nurse if on duty or the coordinator or nurse on call if out of hours. If child
L154@P4: frequently has episodes that deviate from normal parameters action should be
L155@P4: documented in care plan. All staff should be aware of care plan and actions to be taken.
L156@P4: Normal respiratory pattern is an easy, relaxed, subconscious physiological activity
L157@P4: which takes place at a rate dependent on the age and activity of the child.
L158@P4: Where oxygen saturation monitoring is indicated, respiratory assessment and
L159@P4: measurement should be made and recorded simultaneously to give a complete
L160@P4: respiratory assessment.
L161@P4: The pattern, effort and rate of breathing should be observed and recorded as dictated
L162@P4: by plan of care.
L163@P4: Skin colour, pallor, mottling, cyanosis and any traumatic petechiae around the eyelids,
L164@P4: face and neck should be observed and documented.
L165@P4: Infants and children less than six to seven years of age are predominantly abdominal
L166@P4-5: breathers therefore, abdominal movements should be counted.INSERT [Title of SOP, Version & Date]
L167@P5: Signs of respiratory distress e.g., nasal flaring, grunting, wheezing, stridor, dyspnoea,
L168@P5: recession, use of accessory and intercostal muscles, chest shape and movement
L169@P5: should be assessed by looking and listening and findings reported to the named nurse
L170@P5: if on duty or the coordinator or nurse on call if out of hours and documented in the EPR.
L171@P5: The frequency of respiratory assessment and monitoring should be dictated by the
L172@P5: child’s care plan, any immediate actions required following deviation from the norm
L173@P5: should also be highlighted in the care plan. All staff should be familiar with the plan of
L174@P5: care having spent a period of ‘getting to know’ with the child and family. During the GTK
L175@P5: period the normal breathing rates and rhythms of children and young people with
L176@P5: complex needs, will be observed as these can differ from normal parameters.
L177@P5: Guide for normal parameters:
L178@P5: Age rate (breaths per min)
L179@P5: Infants 30-60
L180@P5: Toddlers 24-40
L181@P5: Pre-schoolers 22-34
L182@P5: School-aged children 18-30
L183@P5: Adolescents 12-16
L184@P5: Normal respiratory rates in children (Hazinski 2013)
L185@P5: OXYGEN SATURATION.
L186@P5: Children whose normal oxygen saturations fall outside the normal acceptable limits
L187@P5: should be noted and documented within the EPR for reference to enable staff to report
L188@P5: or escalate concerns correctly.
L189@P5: Where oxygen saturation monitoring is indicated, respiratory assessment and
L190@P5: measurement should be made and recorded simultaneously in order to give a complete
L191@P5: respiratory assessment.
L192@P5: Oxygen saturation and any supplemental oxygen and delivery device should be
L193@P5: recorded in the plan of care.
L194@P5: Oxygen is a drug and requires a written prescription and rationale for use recorded in
L195@P5: the child’s respiratory plan.
L196@P5: If oxygen saturations appear to drop then initially if being used check the device, flow
L197@P5: rate, cylinder or concentrator to ensure optimum oxygenation. In addition, check the
L198@P5: position of the probe is in contact with the skin and has not moved or become
L199@P5-6: dislodged.INSERT [Title of SOP, Version & Date]
L200@P6: Any deviation from identified normal parameters should prompt immediate discussion
L201@P6: with named nurse if on duty or the coordinator or nurse on call if out of hours and
L202@P6: documented in the EPR.
L203@P6: The frequency of oxygen saturation assessment and monitoring should be dictated by
L204@P6: the child’s care plan, any immediate actions required following deviation from the norm
L205@P6: should also be highlighted in the care plan. All staff should be familiar with the plan of
L206@P6: care having spent a period of ‘getting to know’ with the child and family.
L207@P6: Normal oxygen saturations (sats) are between 95%-100% in a well child, we do accept
L208@P6: to 92% any lower than this we would expect SP’s and NA’s to raise concerns with
L209@P6: parents, on-call or the co-ordinator. Some children may have lower accepted oxygen
L210@P6: saturations but this will be specified in the care plan and discussed with SP’s and NA’s
L211@P6: by the named nurse.
L212@P6: PULSE RATE.
L213@P6: Staff working in the CCT team and school teams will only be required to monitor and
L214@P6: record pulse rate that is displayed on a saturation monitor NA’s and SP’s will not be
L215@P6: expected to manually detect pulse rate routinely.
L216@P6: If pulse rate alters or deviates from the norm initially check the position of the probe that
L217@P6: it is in contact with the skin and has not moved or become dislodged.
L218@P6: Any deviation from identified normal parameters should prompt immediate discussion
L219@P6: with named nurse if on duty or the coordinator or nurse on call if out of hours and
L220@P6: documented in the EPR.
L221@P6: The frequency of pulse rate assessment and monitoring should be dictated by the
L222@P6: child’s care plan, any immediate actions required following deviation from the norm
L223@P6: should also be highlighted in the care plan. All staff should be familiar with the plan of
L224@P6: care having spent a period of ‘getting to know’ with the child and family.
L225@P6: Normal heart rates in children (Hazinski 2013)
L226@P6: Age in years
L227@P6: Awake

L229@P6: Sleeping

L231@P6: Neonate 100 -180 80 -160

L234@P6: 100 - 160 75 - 160
L235@P6-7: Toddler 80 - 110 60 - 90INSERT [Title of SOP, Version & Date]
L236@P7: Pre-schooler 70 - 110 60 - 90
L237@P7: School age 65 - 110 60 - 90
L238@P7: Adolescent 60 - 90 50 - 90
L239@P7: TEMPERATURE.
L240@P7: Extremes of temperature- both pyrexia and hypothermia are sensitive markers of acute
L241@P7: illness severity, sepsis and physiological disturbance.
L242@P7: The thermometer should be left in position for the appropriate time, suggested by the
L243@P7: manufacturer’s instructions, to gain an accurate reading.
L244@P7: A normal temperature for babies and children is 36.4C, a high temperature is 38C.
L245@P7: Any deviation from identified normal parameters should prompt immediate discussion
L246@P7: with Named Nurse if on duty or the coordinator or nurse on call if out of hours and
L247@P7: documented in the EPR.
L248@P7: The frequency of temperature assessment and monitoring should be dictated by the
L249@P7: child’s care plan, any immediate actions required following deviation from the norm
L250@P7: should also be highlighted in the care plan. All staff should be familiar with the plan of
L251@P7: care having spent a period of ‘getting to know’ with the child and family.
L252@P7: Body core temperature regarded as 37°C
L253@P7: Pyrexia (fever) is a rise above 37°C
L254@P7: Low grade pyrexia, raised temp up to 38°C
L255@P7: Moderate to high grade pyrexia 38 - 39.9°C
L256@P7: Hyperpyrexia is a temperature ≥ 40⁰C (life threatening)
L257@P7: Hypothermia is a low body temperature below 35 °C.
L258@P7: 7. TRAINING REQUIREMENTS
L259@P7: The named nurse will identify the competency assessments required by the key workers,
L260@P7: ensure these are completed and that appropriate care is provided by the key workers for
L261@P7-8: each individual child and family.INSERT [Title of SOP, Version & Date]
L262@P8: Competency assessments for respiratory rate, oxygen saturations, pulse rate and
L263@P8: temperature recordings will use the LCAT assessments included in the appendix
L264@P8: contained within this SOP.
L265@P8: All SP’s and NA’s will receive a demonstration on how to use any medical devices present
L266@P8: in the child’s home or school for the purpose of recording vital signs or clinical
L267@P8: observations. This will include turning equipment on and off, trouble shooting, applying
L268@P8: probes for oxygen saturation monitoring, correct siting of the thermometer and recording
L269@P8: the value presented. SP’s and NA’s will have opportunities to practice this skill under
L270@P8: supervision prior to having an LCAT assessment of competence.
L271@P8: All staff using medical devices will need to complete the ‘safe use of medical equipment
L272@P8: checklist’ for each piece of equipment used. This will be kept on file in the Diana children’s
L273@P8: community service.
L274@P8: SP’s and NA’s will also receive training and education about the normal values for the
L275@P8: vital signs and clinical observations monitored and recorded.
L276@P8: Individualised care plans will assist SP’s and NA’s to monitor vital signs or clinical
L277@P8: observations according to the child’s need and will give direction of what to report, when
L278@P8: and to whom if vital signs should differ from the norm. One such action may be
L279@P8: telephoning 999 for an emergency ambulance.
